searches.purpose: Locate independent history, foundational participant works, systems concepts and major variants, gender and power critique, broad and diagnosis-bounded outcome reviews, current professional continuation, multi-client ethics and cultural implementation evidence while excluding generic family support, parenting or couples programmes unless the source explicitly places them within a systemic/family intervention review, and while refusing to treat Bowen, structural, strategic, Milan, behavioural, solution-focused or multisystemic models as one standardized protocol

items.title: Um breve histórico da Terapia Familiar Sistêmica: A Brief History of Family Therapy
items.rights_note: Portuguese open-journal article traces the field's context, systems and cybernetic bases, first- and second-order cybernetics, early research and later currents; it is one concise historiography rather than a definitive global origin account.

items.title: Family Therapy in Clinical Practice
items.rights_note: Open Library record for Bowen's collected clinical writings and multigenerational systems programme; the copyrighted book body is not cached or treated as read, and Bowen theory is one branch rather than a synonym for all family therapy.

items.title: Families & Family Therapy
items.rights_note: Open Library edition record and contents for Minuchin's structural family therapy text, including family structure, boundaries, therapeutic joining and restructuring; the copyrighted body is not cached or treated as read, and structural therapy remains a specific branch.

items.title: Family Counseling Approaches
items.rights_note: SAMHSA TIP 39 chapter explains systems principles and several research-based family approaches for substance use disorders; its method descriptions are condition-specific and do not exhaust all family therapy theories or establish efficacy outside SUD care.

items.title: The Problem of Gender in Family Therapy Theory
items.rights_note: Crossref bibliographic record for Hare-Mustin's feminist critique of gender in family therapy theory; the article body and publisher abstract are not treated as read, so this supports discovery and critical coverage rather than detailed claims about her argument.
items.failure_note: The Wiley abstract endpoint returned HTTP 403; the Crossref HTML record was selected without bypassing access controls.

items.title: Family Therapy and Systemic Interventions for Child-Focused Problems: The Current Evidence Base
items.rights_note: Publicly readable copy of Carr's review of meta-analyses, systematic and narrative reviews and controlled trials across multiple child-focused problems; its broad category includes family therapy, parent training and parent-implemented behavioural programmes, so findings cannot be assigned uniformly to every family-therapy branch.

items.title: Couple Therapy and Systemic Interventions for Adult-Focused Problems: The Evidence Base
items.rights_note: Crossref record for the 2025 adult-focused evidence update; the publisher body is not treated as read, and couple therapy plus heterogeneous systemic interventions cannot be collapsed into a single protocol or effect estimate.
items.failure_note: The Wiley full-text endpoint returned HTTP 403; the Crossref HTML record was selected without bypassing access controls.

items.title: Family-Based Mental Health Interventions for Refugees Across the Migration Continuum: A Systematic Review
items.rights_note: CC BY-NC-ND review of ten family-based intervention studies across Global North and South refugee settings identifies parenting, multiple-family and home-visiting models and a limited emerging evidence base; these are not all formal systemic family therapy and cannot establish cross-cultural equivalence.

items.title: AAMFT Code of Ethics
items.rights_note: AAMFT's code effective January 1, 2026 addresses informed consent, multiple clients, confidentiality, power, competence, technology and conflicts of interest; it is a professional ethics standard rather than an adverse-event review and does not replace local law or licensing rules.

items.title: About the American Association for Marriage and Family Therapy
items.rights_note: Current AAMFT page documents professional membership, training, research, ethics and publication functions; a North American association's institutional continuation does not define worldwide systemic practice or validate particular interventions.
